newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EFTA authority withdraws case against Iceland.
newsitem.headline: EFTA authority withdraws case against Iceland.

text.p: The surveillance authority of the European Free Trade Association said on Monday it was withdrawing a case brought against Iceland for failure to comply with agreed tax rules.
In a statement, the authority said there was no longer a reason to seek court judgment on the case since Iceland had effectively removed the discriminatory elements in its commodity taxation.

The authority said that no country belonging to the European Economic Area, which came into force in 1994, was allowed to impose taxes on products from other member countries in excess of that imposed on similar domestic products.
In January, the authority brought proceeedings before the EFTA court as it believed Iceland had failed to adjust its legislation concerning a commodity tax levied on a wide range of products.

"In the authority's view the provisions concerning the basis for the assessment of the tax and the payment of the tax contained elements which had a discriminatory or protective effect in favour of products produced in Iceland," it said.
But it said amendments to Iceland's commodity tax legislation had effectively removed these elements.
